## Overview

The Five Great Generals were the supreme commanders of the Scourge, each commanding multiple Legions and answering only to the supreme command of the Scourge itself. Their names became synonymous with destruction, and entire civilizations came to measure the progress of the war by the movements of these five legendary commanders. Three were defeated by the First Alliance; two vanished from history and were never brought to justice.

---

## The Scourge Hierarchy

### Warbands

A Warband was the most fundamental military unit of the Scourge. Formed around a single powerful warlord, it consisted of the warriors who had sworn — or been forced — to follow their command. Some warbands numbered only a few dozen creatures, while the greatest could field several hundred. Most were composed of a single dominant species, allowing them to exploit their natural strengths and hunting instincts with ruthless efficiency.

Warbands were expected to wage constant campaigns, conquer territory, and challenge rival commanders. Success was rewarded with prestige, resources, and most importantly the right to claim the defeated army through the ancient tradition known as **The Gathering of the Spoils**.

### Legions

As victorious warbands continued to absorb their rivals, they eventually grew beyond the ability of a single commander to lead them as a unified hunting force. At this point they were reorganized into Legions. Unlike warbands, a Legion was not simply a larger army — it was an entire military host.

Each Legion united numerous warbands beneath a single Great General, preserving the independence of individual warlords while coordinating them toward a common military objective. Every warband retained its own identity, traditions, and commanding warlord, but all ultimately answered to the General who commanded the Legion.

This structure proved remarkably effective. Rather than forcing wildly different monstrous species into identical formations, the Scourge allowed each warband to fight according to its own strengths while the Legion's command ensured that every assault formed part of a far greater strategy. Creatures that would have been incapable of cooperating on their own became devastatingly efficient when directed by a General capable of orchestrating dozens of warbands simultaneously.

### The Five Great Generals

The Five Great Generals commanded multiple Legions and answered only to the supreme command of the Scourge itself. Their campaigns were not merely regional threats — they were existential crises for entire civilizations.

---

## The Gathering of the Spoils

The Gathering of the Spoils was the ancient law that governed conflicts within the Scourge. When two great war generals sought to claim one another's forces, neither was permitted to simply overwhelm the other through numbers. Instead, their leaders would meet in single combat. No armies. No champions. No interference. Two warriors entered and one warrior left.

The victor claimed the defeated general's forces as their own. To the Scourge, the fallen army was not destroyed — it became spoils: soldiers without a master, waiting for a stronger will to give them purpose once more. The tradition served more than ritual. It ensured that the armies of the Scourge remained in the hands of those capable of commanding them. Strength earned obedience, while weakness invited replacement.

But victory through the Gathering offered more than command. Every defeated general left behind soldiers, weapons, territories, knowledge, and creatures willing — or forced — to serve whoever had proven themselves worthy. Over centuries, some warlords accumulated large enough forces to rival kingdoms. Among all those who rose through the Gathering, few left behind a name as feared as Khar'Zul.

---

## The Five Generals

### I. Khar'Zul, The Flesh That Remembers
**Species:** Ulrath
**Legion:** One of the largest Legions ever assembled — extraordinary diversity of monstrous races
**Role:** Master tactician; viewed war as an art to be perfected
**Fate:** Defeated and sealed within his own greatsword. The last of the three Generals to fall.

### II. Voragos, The Ashen Winged Eclipse
**Species:** Ancient Black Dragon
**Legion:** The Ashen Legion — aerial assault, speed, devastation
**Role:** Living instrument of annihilation; deployed only when conquest ceased to matter
**Fate:** Slain by the First Alliance. The first Great General to fall.

### III. Xerathul, The Veiled Eyes of Death
**Species:** Lich
**Legion:** The Grave Legion — undead army that grew stronger with every battle
**Role:** Master of necromancy; measured success through attrition
**Fate:** Hunted down and slain after Voragos. The second General to fall.

### IV. Vaessra, The Whisper Before Ruin
**Species:** Fallen Empyrean
**Legion:** The Twilight Legion — infiltration, corruption, subversion
**Role:** Destroyed kingdoms from within; battles often won before swords were drawn
**Fate:** Vanished without explanation before Voragos fell. Never found.

### V. Kha'Thuun, The Witness from Beyond
**Species:** Mind Flayer
**Legion:** The Black Legion — intelligence gathering, psionic operatives
**Role:** Supreme intelligence; ensured every campaign began with overwhelming informational superiority
**Fate:** Vanished as the Scourge lost ground. Never defeated. Never found.

---

## Current Status

- **Khar'Zul**: Sealed within his blade, carried by Balor Skallfang
- **Voragos**: Deceased — slain in the bloodiest battle of the Scourge War
- **Xerathul**: Deceased — hunted down and destroyed
- **Vaessra**: Unknown — vanished, possibly still exists under another name
- **Kha'Thuun**: Unknown — vanished with countless secrets
